mainTopic: Taking back land given for a debt, when a creditor earns the פירות, and a rented cow that is lent out and dies
overview: The amud opens with a מחלוקת between רב אחא and רבינא. A debtor hands his land to his creditor on his own, without בית דין. Can he pay later and take it back? One view says it is a full sale. The other says he gave it only out of embarrassment, so it is returned like a שומא. Next, רבה, אביי, and רבא disagree about the moment a creditor collecting land through בית דין may start eating its פירות. Then a new משנה teaches that when a שוכר lends a rented cow to a שואל and it dies naturally, the שוכר swears and the שואל pays him; רבי יוסי says the payment goes to the owner. אביי explains that the שוכר's right begins at the cow's death, and the oath only reassures the owner. רבי זירא shows how an owner who keeps borrowing back his rented cow may owe several cows; רבינא defends this, and מר בר רב אשי says only two cows are owed. The amud ends as רבי ירמיה begins discussing when the שוכר and שואל must bring a חטאת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Debtor hands over land himself: can it be returned?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue whether land the debtor gave over on his own can be reclaimed once he pays the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the debtor himself gave the creditor his land for the debt, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says it goes back to him, and one says it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case: the debtor handed over his land on his own, with no court involved. Two אמוראים argue whether he can later pay the money and take the land back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא taught that land taken through a court appraisal (שומא) can be returned if the debtor pays. The question here is whether that rule also covers land the debtor gave over by himself. One opinion says yes and the other says no.

keyTerms.meaning: He collected it for him (here: the debtor himself gave the land over)
It goes back (the land is returned)

phrases.english: If he himself handed it over to him for his debt,
phrases.notes: "He himself" means the debtor, acting on his own instead of having בית דין do it.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagree about it.
One says: it goes back,
phrases.notes: "It" is the appraisal (שומא) from the line before, which can be undone when the debtor pays.

phrases.english: and one says: it does not go back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the earlier rule that a שומא can be returned to a new case: the debtor gave the land over by himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: one view says the land returns once the debt is paid, and the other says it does not.

steps.title: Why it does not go back: a full sale
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that the land is not returned treats the handover as a real, complete sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it does not go back holds that this is a full sale, because the debtor handed it over by his own choice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the opinion that the land stays with the creditor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court appraisal is forced on the debtor, so the law lets him undo it. Here the debtor chose on his own to give the land. That makes it like an ordinary sale, and you cannot take back a sale.

phrases.english: The one who says it does not go back holds:
this is a full sale,
since he gave it over of his own free will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the second opinion in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A voluntary handover counts as a full sale, so the land is not returned.

steps.title: Why it does go back: he only gave it out of embarrassment
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that the land is returned says the handover was not a true sale. The debtor gave it only to avoid the shame of being taken to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it goes back holds that it is not a full sale. He gave it over himself and did not go to court only because he was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side: why the land is returned even though the debtor gave it over himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion agrees that the debtor acted on his own. But it says his choice was not a real wish to sell. He only wanted to avoid being dragged to בית דין. So it is really the same as a court collection, and it can be undone like a שומא.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אחא and רבינא argue about land the debtor gave over on his own. One says it is a real sale and is not returned. The other says he gave it only out of embarrassment, so it is returned like a שומא.

phrases.english: And the one who says it goes back holds:
it is not a full sale,
and the fact that he gave it over on his own
and did not come to court:
it was because of embarrassment that he gave it over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning of the first opinion and answers the logic of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handover done to avoid embarrassment is not a true sale, so the land is returned.

steps.title: From when does the creditor eat the produce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what moment the creditor who collects land becomes entitled to its פירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when does he eat the produce?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about land collected for a debt. It is setting up three answers that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting land through בית דין takes several stages. The question is which stage makes the land the creditor's, so that its produce belongs to him.

phrases.english: And from when does he eat the produce?
phrases.notes: "He" is the creditor who is collecting the debtor's land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether collected land can be returned to when the creditor's ownership begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The moment from which the פירות of collected land belong to the creditor.

steps.title: רבה: once the collection document reaches him
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the produce is his from when the אדרכתא arrives in his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: from when the אדרכתא reaches his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the first answer: the creditor eats the produce once he physically receives the court's collection document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אדרכתא is the court document that lets the creditor take the debtor's property. For רבה, the land becomes the creditor's when that document comes into his own hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Court document authorizing collection from the debtor's property

phrases.english: Rabba said:
From when the authorization document reaches his hand.
phrases.notes: An אדרכתא is the court paper that lets the creditor go and take the debtor's land.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: מִכִּי מָטְיָא אַדְרַכְתָּא לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The creditor eats the produce from when the אדרכתא reaches him.

steps.title: אביי: the witnesses' signatures acquire it for him
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the creditor does not need to receive the document. Once the witnesses sign, the land is already his.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: his witnesses, through their signatures, acquire it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives an earlier starting point than רבה: the moment the witnesses sign the אדרכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה waits until the document is in the creditor's hands. אביי says the witnesses' signing is already enough to acquire the land on the creditor's behalf. So the produce is his from the signing, even before he gets the paper.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Its witnesses, with their signatures, acquire for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: עֵדָיו בַּחֲתוּמָיו זָכִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבה and gives an earlier moment.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The creditor gets the produce from when the witnesses sign the אדרכתא.

steps.title: רבא: once the days of proclamation are over
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the produce is the creditor's only after the public proclamation period ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: from when the days of proclamation are finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the latest starting point. The produce belongs to the creditor only after בית דין finishes publicly announcing the land for sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the land goes to the creditor, בית דין announces it publicly, and someone else might buy it. So for רבא, the land is not surely the creditor's until the announcement days are over.

keyTerms.meaning: Public proclamation (announcing the land for sale)

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on when the creditor eats the produce: רבה says when the אדרכתא reaches him, אביי says when the witnesses sign it, and רבא says when the proclamation days end.

phrases.english: Rava said:
From when the days of proclamation are completed.
phrases.notes: This is the period when בית דין publicly announces the land for sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִכִּי שְׁלִימוּ יְמֵי אַכְרַזְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view, later than both רבה and אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The creditor gets the produce only after the proclamation period ends.

steps.title: A rented cow is lent out and dies naturally
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the שוכר swears to the owner that the cow died naturally, and the שואל pays the שוכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone rents a cow and lends it to another person, and it dies naturally, the renter swears it died naturally, and the borrower pays the renter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a case of a rented cow that was passed on to a borrower and then died naturally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוכר does not pay when an animal dies naturally, so he only has to swear to the owner. A שואל does pay even when it dies naturally. The משנה says the borrower's payment goes to the שוכר, not to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: A renter, someone who pays to use an item
A borrower, someone who uses an item for free
Died in its normal way, of natural causes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. The שוכר is exempt when the cow dies naturally and only swears. The שואל is liable even then, and he pays the שוכר.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who rents a cow from his fellow
and lent it to another person,
and it died in its normal way –
the renter swears that it died in its normal way,
and the borrower pays the renter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, after the previous discussion about a creditor collecting land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שוכר swears to the owner that the cow died naturally, and the שואל pays the שוכר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי says the payment goes back to the owner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי objects that the שוכר should not make a profit from someone else's cow. The payment should go to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: How can the renter make money from another person's cow? Rather, the cow goes back to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first ruling of the משנה and gives his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first view, the שוכר gets paid for a cow that was never his. רבי יוסי calls this doing business with someone else's property, so the payment from the שואל belongs to the owner.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions in the משנה. The תנא קמא says the שואל pays the שוכר. רבי יוסי says the payment goes to the owner.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
How can that one do business
with his fellow's cow?
Rather, the cow goes back to the owner.
phrases.notes: He means the value of the cow that the borrower pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כֵּיצַד הַלָּה עוֹשֶׂה סְחוֹרָה בְּפָרָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of the first opinion in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שוכר may not profit from the owner's cow, so the borrower's payment goes to the owner.

steps.title: The שוכר acquires the cow through his oath
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין suggests to אביי that the שוכר gains the right to the cow by taking the שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said to אביי: After all, how does the renter acquire this cow? With the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and sets up the next move. רב אידי בר אבין explains how the שוכר earns the right to be paid, and the next step will challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the תנא קמא, the שוכר receives payment for a cow that was not his. רב אידי בר אבין assumes this is because his oath to the owner gives him the right to it.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, a word that opens a basic assumption

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said to Abaye:
After all, with what does the renter acquire
this cow? With the oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, שׂוֹכֵר בְּמַאי קָנֵי לְהַאי פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines how the first ruling of the משנה in step 8 works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The working assumption is that the שוכר acquires the cow through his oath.

steps.title: Why can't the owner skip the renter and sue the borrower?
steps.stepSummary: If the oath is what gives the שוכר his rights, the owner could refuse the oath and go to court with the שואל himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the owner say to the renter: Forget you and forget your oath, and I will go to court with the borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the assumption from the last step, the גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that the שואל pays the שוכר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שוכר only gains the cow by swearing, the owner can stop that from happening by saying he does not want the oath. Then the cow never passes to the שוכר, and the owner could collect from the שואל directly. That would make the משנה's ruling empty.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who rents out the item, the owner

phrases.english: So let the owner who rented it out say to the renter:
Remove yourself and remove your oath,
phrases.notes: Basically: I don't want your oath, and I'm leaving you out of this.

phrases.english: and I will go to court with the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵימָא לֵיהּ מַשְׂכִּיר לְשׂוֹכֵר: דַּל אַנְתְּ וְדַל שְׁבוּעֲתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a challenge on the assumption from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the שואל pays the שוכר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the oath creates the שוכר's rights, the owner can refuse the oath and collect from the שואל himself.

steps.title: אביי: the renter acquires at the moment of death
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the שוכר gains the right at the moment the cow dies. The oath is only there to reassure the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think the renter acquires it with the oath? He acquires it from the moment it dies, and the oath is just to put the owner's mind at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by rejecting the idea that the oath is what gives the שוכר his rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moment the cow dies, the שוכר's right to the payment is already set. The oath does not create anything. It only reassures the owner that the שוכר was not careless. So the owner cannot cancel the שוכר's rights by refusing the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: To calm his mind, to reassure him

steps.whatToRemember: The שוכר's right to the payment begins when the cow dies, not when he swears. The שבועה only reassures the owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the right comes from the death itself, the owner has no way to cut the שוכר out. This is what keeps the משנה's ruling in place.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רב אידי בר אבין.

phrases.english: Do you think

phrases.aramaic: שׂוֹכֵר בִּשְׁבוּעָה הוּא דְּקָא קָנֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: that it is with the oath that the renter acquires it?
It is from the moment of death that he acquires it.
And the oath is to put at ease the mind
of the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ, שׂוֹכֵר בִּשְׁבוּעָה הוּא דְּקָא קָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by rejecting the assumption of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise behind the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שוכר acquires through the oath, so the owner could refuse the oath and sue the שואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שוכר acquires at the moment of death. The oath only reassures the owner, so refusing it changes nothing.

steps.title: Sometimes the owner pays the renter several cows
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says there are cases where the owner himself pays the שוכר several cows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Sometimes the owner pays several cows to the renter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא makes a surprising statement based on the משנה's rule. It sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a שואל pays the שוכר when the cow dies. רבי זירא points out that this rule can even make the owner pay the שוכר, and more than one cow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
There are times when the owner pays
several cows to the renter.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּעָמִים שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים מְשַׁלְּמִין כַּמָּה פָּרוֹת לַשּׂוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה's rule, now settled by אביי, to describe an unusual result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In some cases the owner pays the שוכר several cows.

steps.title: The case of renting and borrowing back and forth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes the case. The owner keeps borrowing back his own cow, which has been rented out, and he owes a cow for each time he borrowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? The renter rented it from the owner for 100 days, then the owner borrowed it from him for 90 days. Then the renter rented it again for 80 days, and the owner borrowed it again for 70 days. The cow died during the borrowing days, so for each borrowing the owner owes one cow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case רבי זירא means, and then lays it out step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the cow is rented out, the owner who borrows it back is a שואל toward the שוכר. A שואל must pay if the cow dies. Since the owner borrowed it twice, each borrowing makes him liable for one cow.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does this happen?

steps.whatToRemember: An owner who borrows back his own rented cow counts as a שואל. If it dies, he must pay the שוכר. He owes a separate cow for each borrowing.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep track of who is who. The owner of the cow is the one doing the borrowing here, so he is the one who pays.

phrases.english: What is the case?
He rented it from him for a hundred days,
and then he borrowed it from him for ninety days,
phrases.notes: Now it flips: the owner borrows his own cow back from the renter.

phrases.english: then he rented it from him again for eighty days,
and then he borrowed it from him for seventy days,
and it died within the days of its borrowing,
so that for each and every borrowing
he is liable for one cow.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אַגְרַהּ מִינֵּיהּ מְאָה יוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case behind רבי זירא's statement in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can an owner end up paying several cows to the renter?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the renting and borrowing alternate and the cow dies while the owner has it on loan, he owes one cow for each borrowing.

steps.title: It is only one cow going back and forth
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges רבינא. It is one cow that just switches between being rented and being borrowed, so how can the owner owe many cows?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: After all, it is just one cow. He keeps bringing it in and taking it out. He takes it out of renting and puts it into borrowing, then takes it out of borrowing and puts it back into renting. So why should he owe more than one cow?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי pushes back on the idea from Step 14 that the owner owes a separate cow for each time he borrowed it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that each new borrowing simply replaces the earlier status. When the owner borrows the cow, it leaves the 'rental' status, and when he rents it out again, it leaves the 'borrowing' status. If there is only ever one cow, piling up many debts seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: After all; since (a word that opens a logical challenge)
He brought it in and took it out (moved it from one status to another)
Renting (the renter pays for the use of the animal)
Borrowing (the borrower uses it for free)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
After all, it is one cow,
he brought it in and took it out;
phrases.notes: The owner moved the cow from one legal status into another; he didn't physically move it.

phrases.english: he took it out of renting and brought it into borrowing;
he took it out of borrowing and brought it into renting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the outcome in Step 14 that the owner owes a cow for each borrowing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner owes the שוכר several cows.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is physically only one cow, and each new status cancels the one before it. So it seems there should be only one debt.

steps.title: The cow is dead, so the owner cannot just hand it back
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that since the cow died, the owner cannot say 'here is your cow.' So each promise he made stands on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: But is the cow still standing here, so that the owner could say this to him ('here is your cow')?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends the idea that the owner owes several cows by pointing out that the cow no longer exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Switching statuses back and forth would only matter if the owner could give the actual cow back. Since it died, he cannot do that. So he is stuck owing everything he took on, one cow for each borrowing.

keyTerms.meaning: Intact; still in its original state
But is it there? (a question that expects the answer 'no')

phrases.english: He said to him:
But is the cow still there intact
that he could say this to him?

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a fact the challenge ignored: the cow has died.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since it is one cow moving between statuses, there should be only one debt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'one cow' argument works only if the cow can be returned. Since it is dead, each obligation remains, and the owner owes a cow for each one.

steps.title: Only two cows: one for borrowing, one for renting
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says the owner owes only two cows. One for the borrowing, which the שוכר keeps for good, and one for the rental, which he uses until the rental ends and then returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: The renter can claim only two cows from him, one for the borrowing and one for the renting. All the borrowings count as one type, and all the rentings count as one type. The cow for the borrowing, the renter owns completely. The cow for the renting, he works with during his rental days and then gives back to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי offers a different view. He says the owner does not owe a cow for every single borrowing, only two cows in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He groups the obligations by type rather than counting each time. All the borrowings make one borrower's debt, so the owner must replace the cow fully, and the שוכר keeps it. All the rentals make one rental duty, so the owner must give the שוכר a cow to use for the rest of the rental period, and it then goes back to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of his rental period

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on how many cows the owner owes. רבי זירא, defended by רבינא: one for each borrowing, because the cow is dead and cannot be handed back. מר בר רב אשי: only two, one kept for good for the borrowing and one used and returned for the rental.
steps.confusionAlert: The two cows are not treated the same. The borrowing cow becomes the שוכר's forever. The rental cow is only used for the rental period and then goes back to the owner.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ עֲלֵיהֶן אֶלָּא שְׁתֵּי פָּרוֹת,
phrases.english: He has a claim against him for only two cows,
phrases.notes: Literally 'against them.' He means the renter's claim against the owner for all those borrowings put together.

phrases.english: one for the borrowing and one for the renting.
The category of borrowing is one,
and the category of renting is one.
The one for borrowing, he acquires completely;
the one for renting, he works with it for his rental days,
and returns it to its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֵין לוֹ עֲלֵיהֶן אֶלָּא שְׁתֵּי פָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the outcome defended in Step 16 and offers a middle position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner owes only two cows. One for the borrowing, kept permanently by the שוכר. One for the rental, used until the rental ends and then returned to the owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that repeated acts of the same legal type can be counted as one obligation instead of many.

steps.title: Sometimes both must bring a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה begins a new statement about the משנה's cases: there are times when both the שוכר and the שואל are liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: There are times when both of them are liable to bring a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic connected to the משנה's cases. רבי ירמיה opens a statement about when both people must bring a חטאת. This line is setting up his explanation, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about money: who owes a cow to whom. רבי ירמיה shifts to the offerings that come from the oaths in these cases. He signals that there are several possible outcomes, starting with one where both are liable.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
There are times that both are liable to a sin-offering,
phrases.notes: 'Both' means the שוכר and the שואל from the משנה's case. His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: פְּעָמִים שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם בְּחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the money discussion and opens a new discussion about the offerings connected to the משנה's cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are cases in which both the שוכר and the שואל are liable to bring a חטאת. The details continue on the next amud.
